I will keep my land in the usual wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the crop pattern I know best, the machinery matches it, seed and fertilizer are easy to buy, and selling grain is straightforward. At my age, I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or take on labor-heavy field work. I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the ground, manage it steadily through spring with one topdressing and a few irrigations depending on moisture, then harvest it in early summer. Right after wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land so the field does not sit idle.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want better stand and more even yield without making management complicated. I will keep fertilizer moderate and balanced instead of chasing very high yield, because too much nitrogen causes lodging and wastes money. I will irrigate only when the crop truly needs it, mainly around jointing and grain filling if the soil is dry. I will spray only as needed for weeds, aphids, rust, or other common diseases. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because local hybrid maize is stable and productive. I will sow quickly after wheat harvest, use basal fertilizer plus some nitrogen support, and watch the field in the seedling and tasseling stages. I will keep the whole plan simple, mechanized, and low-risk, because that is what I would do for steady income and manageable work this year.
